transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
President Trump's recent effort to impose a limited ceasefire on energy targets has collapsed.
The president earlier claimed Russia had agreed to a ceasefire and urged Ukraine to do the same.
Neither side complied.
Meanwhile, at least one person has been killed and five others injured after Ukraine carried out waves of drone strikes against Russia's former imperial capital, St. Petersburg.
NPR's Charles Mains has the latest from Moscow.
According to Russia's regional governor, Ukrainian drones struck a range of strategic targets in St. Petersburg, including the city's port oil terminal and a refinery.
The attacks follow a similar targeting of a key oil facility that services the capital, Moscow, earlier this week.
President Trump has condemned Ukraine for resuming strikes on Russian oil facilities.
That criticism, coming days after Trump announced a deal to purchase Russian diesel fuel in an attempt to tamp down gas prices in the U.S. ahead of midterm elections.
Ukraine's president, Vladimir Zelensky, says he was forced to abandon Trump's declared energy truce, noting Russia had never paused its attacks on Ukraine's heating and electrical systems.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
President Trump made a campaign stop in Kentucky yesterday, where he threw his support behind Republicans facing tight midterm races.
Zach Carion reports from member station WVXU in Cincinnati.
Trump says if Republicans lose, Democrats will undo his administration's work from its first two years back in office.
That's why he says these midterms are important in solid red Kentucky and in nearby Ohio, where Democrats could make gains.
If they win the midterms, all of a sudden you're going to see a slide and all of the crap that we talk about, the incompetent stuff that we talk about is going to come back and we're going to go through the same process.
And I don't think our country can handle it again.
Kentucky Republicans are expected to win their races, but in Ohio, GOP candidates are in tougher battles like incumbent Senator John Husted, who's facing former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown.
For NPR News, I'm Zach Carion in Highland Heights, Kentucky.
Wall Street investors are bracing for earnings from major companies like Netflix and Meta this week.
NPR's Rafael Naum has a preview.
In a week that's light in terms of economic data, the quarterly earnings reports should provide investors a good sense of how some companies are faring in an uncertain economy.
Netflix, for example, has recently announced layoffs amid concerns about whether the company can continue to keep its subscribers spending significant time on its platform.
Meanwhile, Meta is releasing earnings amid rising concerns about whether the massive investments in AI will pay off.
And Tesla is set to report how many deliveries it accomplished in the latest quarter, a key metric of demand for the company's vehicles.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
This is NPR.
Officials from Congo say the Ebola outbreak has spread to an eighth province.
This comes as Kenya has announced four new cases.
As Michael Kologie reports, this brings the total number of confirmed cases in the East African nation to seven.
In a statement yesterday, Kenyan authorities said that all four patients were already in quarantine when they developed symptoms,
adding that tests confirmed they have the Bundebugia strain of Ebola.
The statement noted that one of the four is a close male relative of the first Ebola patient in the country,
who passed away earlier this month after travelling from the Democratic Republic of Congo to Kenya through Uganda.
Health officials said that the additional three new cases are health workers who had attended to the first Ebola patient,
with authorities noting that the three are receiving supportive care at a designated facility.
For NPR News, I'm Michael Kologie in Nairobi.
China is taking steps to restrict or outright ban exports of 40 technologies, including AI, chips and solar power.
The proposal includes restrictions or outright bans on 23 AI technologies.
This move comes as the tech race continues with countries including the United States.
China's Ministry of Commerce, together with the Ministry of Science and Technology,
both call the move necessary for China's national security.
Meanwhile, the U.S. has imposed restrictions on exports of advanced technologies to China,
along with regulations on access to Chinese products.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

Ukrainian drones strike St. Petersburg oil terminal and refinery, killing at least one person
Trump criticizes Ukraine's renewed strikes on Russian oil facilities after Russian diesel deal
Trump campaigns in Kentucky for Republicans in tight midterm races, warns Democrats would reverse his work
Wall Street braces for earnings from Netflix, Meta, and Tesla amid economic uncertainty
Ebola outbreak spreads to an eighth province in Congo
Kenya reports four new Ebola cases, bringing its total confirmed to seven
